data.name: Eashwar
data.gender_notes: Eashwar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Eashwar is a name derived from Sanskrit language. It is a form of Lord Shiva, the supreme deity in Hinduism, representing creation, destruction, and regeneration. Eashwar is the preserver of the universe and is believed to be the god of fertility, prosperity, and auspiciousness. The name Eashwar carries the meaning “Lord of the Creation” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Eashwar usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the creation and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes divine power, creation, and the cycle of life.
data.etymology: Eashwar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Creation.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Eashwar total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Eashwar denotes a strong connection to Hindu heritage and holds immense significance in Hindu mythology. This name is revered and chanted in various rituals and traditions, indicating a deep reverence and respect towards Lord Shiva. It is not uncommon to see temples and deities being named after Eashwar. People often seek blessings of Eashwar during important stages of life, such as marriages, births, and graduations.
data.spiritual_significance: Eashwar is a symbol of supreme power and the ultimate creator and destroyer of the universe. It signifies the unity of all deities, as Lord Shiva is often considered the embodiment of spiritual disciplines and knowledge. The name Eashwar reminds us of the infinite cycles of birth, death, and rebirth, and the ultimate role of self-realization and enlightenment in spiritual growth. It is a reminder of our interconnectedness to the universe and the importance of surgeing internal peace and harmony.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Eashwar is a name of Lord Shiva, symbolizing the controller of all creation and destruction. He is the embodiment of compassion and grace, bestowing blessings upon devotees.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Eashwar is a name of Lord Shiva, the Hindu god of destruction. The name Eashwar carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
